skill.name: python-appservice-deploy
skill.description: Guides AI agents through deploying Python Flask, Django, FastAPI, or generic apps to Azure App Service Linux using Azure CLI or azd.
skill.summary: Deploy Python web apps to Azure App Service Linux with framework detection and repeatable deployment steps.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, Azure CLI snippets, placeholders, or benign device references, so they were adjudicated as false positives. I confirmed the retry wrapper command execution paths because they run caller-provided command strings through eval or PowerShell -Command. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Retry wrappers execute concatenated command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval and powershell -Command with argument arrays or a fixed allowlist of Azure commands and parameters.

remediation.issue: User-provided Azure resource values may be interpolated into shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Validate app, resource group, plan, region, and subscription values before use, and reject shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: The workflow creates paid Azure resources without explicit confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require a clear user confirmation that names the subscription, region, SKU, and resources before creation.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Command Strings in Retry Wrappers
semantic_findings.description: The workflow permits user-supplied Azure values, while retry wrappers execute whole command strings through eval or PowerShell -Command. Unsafe interpolation could allow shell metacharacters to run as commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts accept full command strings and execute them dynamically. The deployment guide says to use user-requested resource values verbatim, so injection depends on caller escaping.

semantic_findings.title: Billable Azure Resources Created Without Explicit Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The guide derives resource names, prints defaults, and tells the agent not to ask for confirmation before creating a P0v3 App Service plan and web app. This can spend money or change cloud state after a single deployment request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly skip confirmation and create or reuse paid Azure resources. This is intentional deployment behavior, but it is a marketplace safety risk.

content.user_title: Deploy Python Apps to Azure App Service
content.value_statement: Azure App Service deployments require runtime, startup, and deploy path choices. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable Python deployment flow.
actual_capabilities: Detects Flask, Django, FastAPI, generic WSGI, generic ASGI, or unknown Python projects.
Chooses the azd flow when azure.yaml targets Azure App Service.
Creates or reuses a resource group, App Service plan, and Python web app.
Configures server-side build and framework-specific startup behavior.
Packages and deploys code through az webapp deploy or azd deploy.
Prints the App Service URL and log commands after deployment.
limitations: Supports Azure App Service Linux for Python projects only.
Does not design infrastructure for containers, Functions, databases, networks, or IaC.
Does not perform post-deploy health checks or HTTP probes.
Requires Azure CLI or azd authentication in the user environment.

use_cases.title: Ship a Flask Site
use_cases.description: Deploy a small Flask app with default Azure resource names and Oryx build settings.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Deployments
use_cases.description: Apply the same App Service plan, runtime, and deployment sequence across Python services.

use_cases.title: Guide an AI Coding Agent
use_cases.description: Give an agent precise Azure CLI or azd steps for a Python App Service deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Flask App
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this Flask project to Azure App Service. Use safe defaults and ask me only for the app name if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a FastAPI App
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this FastAPI project to Azure App Service and configure the correct startup behavior for the detected entry point.

prompt_templates.title: Use an Existing azd Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Deployment from a repository that already has Azure Developer CLI files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this repository has an App Service azure.yaml file. If it does, deploy with azd and report the endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Failed Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my failed Python App Service deployment, identify whether it is transient or configuration-related, and recommend the next safe step.

output_examples.input: Deploy my FastAPI project with default Azure resources.
output_examples.output: The skill reports FastAPI detection, configures explicit startup behavior, enables server-side build, deploys the app, and returns the App Service URL.

output_examples.input: Deploy a Django app that already has azure.yaml.
output_examples.output: The skill checks whether azure.yaml targets App Service, uses azd when appropriate, and stops after reporting the deployed endpoint.

output_examples.input: My deployment failed with a transient Azure error.
output_examples.output: The skill distinguishes transient platform errors from configuration errors and suggests a limited retry flow for resource creation.

best_practices: Confirm the Azure subscription and app name before creating resources.
Keep secrets out of deployment packages and application source files.
Use the generated URL and wait window before judging app startup.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for Container Apps, Functions, or non-Python workloads.
Do not include virtual environments, caches, or .env files in deployment packages.
Do not treat an early HTTP error as proof that deployment failed.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a resource group, App Service plan, and web app when they are missing.

faq.question: Does it support containers or Azure Functions?
faq.answer: No. It is scoped to Python apps on Azure App Service Linux.

faq.question: Can it use Azure Developer CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses azd when azure.yaml targets App Service.

faq.question: Does it verify the live site after deployment?
faq.answer: No. It stops after deployment and tells the user to wait before opening the site.

faq.question: How does it handle FastAPI apps?
faq.answer: It sets explicit uvicorn startup behavior instead of relying on automatic platform detection.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: The user must already be signed in to Azure CLI or azd with access to the target subscription.
